evals.prompt: I'm building a Laravel app where users can earn and spend credits (like a points/rewards system). Users earn credits when they make purchases and can spend them as discounts. I need to be able to see a full history of every credit transaction and the current balance. What's the best way to model this?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Event Sourcing as the right pattern, explains why (immutable audit trail, balance = sum of events), recommends spatie/laravel-event-sourcing or hirethunk/verbs, provides a concrete example with events like CreditEarned and CreditSpent, and shows how to implement an aggregate or equivalent.
assertions: Recommends Event Sourcing as the primary approach (not plain Eloquent CRUD with a transactions table)
Names a specific library: spatie/laravel-event-sourcing or hirethunk/verbs
Shows an event class representing a credit transaction (e.g., CreditEarned, CreditAdded, MoneyAdded or similar)
Explains that balance is derived from events (not stored directly)
Mentions the immutable audit trail / full history as a key benefit

evals.prompt: We have an Order model with a status field. Right now it's just a string but we keep getting bugs where orders end up in impossible states — like a delivered order getting set back to pending. We want to enforce that status transitions only happen in valid sequences. How do we do this properly in Laravel?
evals.expected_output: Recommends spatie/laravel-model-states, explains state machine concepts (defined transitions, CouldNotPerformTransition exception on invalid transitions), shows how to create State base class with StateConfig defining allowed transitions, and how to perform transitions.
assertions: Recommends spatie/laravel-model-states specifically
Shows StateConfig with allowTransition() defining the valid transition graph
Shows concrete State subclasses (Pending, Confirmed, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled or similar)
Mentions that invalid transitions throw an exception
Shows HasStates trait and status cast on the Order model

evals.prompt: We're about to launch a major redesign of our checkout flow. We don't want to roll it out to everyone at once — we want to test it with 5% of users first, then gradually increase. Some of our team also needs to always see the new version for QA. What's the cleanest way to handle this in Laravel?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Laravel Pennant as the primary solution, shows Feature::define() with percentage rollout logic and staff override, explains that values are stored after first resolution (database driver), shows blade directives and how to activate/deactivate for specific users.
assertions: Recommends Laravel Pennant as the primary solution
Shows Feature::define() with percentage rollout logic
Addresses the staff/QA requirement — internal users always see the new version
Shows how to check the flag in code (Feature::active() or @feature blade directive)
Mentions ability to manually activate/deactivate for specific users

evals.prompt: I have a subscription model that goes through states: trialing, active, past_due, paused, cancelled. Different actions are allowed depending on the state (e.g., you can only pause an active subscription). Should I use a state machine or event sourcing for this? Can you show me how to set it up?
evals.expected_output: Correctly recommends State Machine (not Event Sourcing) for this use case — the transitions are the key logic, not audit history. Shows spatie/laravel-model-states setup with a Subscription model, concrete state classes for each status, and StateConfig with allowed transitions.
assertions: Correctly recommends State Machine as the primary approach (not Event Sourcing)
Explains WHY state machine fits better — enforcing valid transitions is the core requirement
Recommends spatie/laravel-model-states
Shows state classes for subscription lifecycle (Trialing, Active, PastDue, Paused, Cancelled)
Shows the valid transition graph for a subscription
